At the same time today, the international community has another opportunity to send the proper signal to the parties to the conflict, albeit in the form of a General Assembly resolution. This draft presented by Spain contains the main provisions from the document that was vetoed last week, a demand for an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire, the release of all hostages, and lifting the blockade on Gaza. Its aims are exclusively humanitarian in nature and focus on the most important thing, ending the slaughter that is claiming more and more human lives in the Gaza Strip. In that future, there is no place for forced displacements, demographic or territorial changes, the construction of illegal settlements, just as there is also no place for terrorism and violence. Mr. President, Russia will vote in favour of this draft resolution and calls for the same from all those who, not in words but in deeds, are in favour of a prompt resolution of the most protracted conflict in the world, without which achieving a lasting peace and prosperity in the Middle East will remain a mirage. Moreover, the adoption of this document will give the right momentum to the high-level conference on the Middle East peace process that will begin next week. Mr. President, the United States will support a future for the people in Gaza that is free of Hamas and full of opportunity. That is why we recognise the negotiating efforts carried out by Egypt, Qatar and the US to make progress in this difficult situation, and we hope that this will see success soon. It is difficult to attain tangible results. We understand the concerns of those in the conflict who need to be represented for the purposes of peace in this organisation. Thank you, President. The UK is deeply concerned by ongoing Israeli operations in the West Bank, including incidents where children have been killed. This is appalling and unacceptable. Israeli government policies which have completely blocked or severely restricted humanitarian aid are unacceptable. That civilians have been killed while desperately trying to feed their families is inhumane and the UK rejects any attempts at demographic or territorial change in the Gaza Strip. I thank the distinguished representative of the United Kingdom. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of the Republic of Korea.

Mr. President, as a Security Council member, The Republic of Korea has reiterated its deep concerns over the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza. Heading toward the high-level conference.

I thank the distinguished representative of the Republic of Korea. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Seychelles.

Well, thank you, Mr. President, and allow me first to express our deep concern regarding the grave humanitarian situation unfolding in Gaza. Czechia supports efforts to find a meaningful and durable resolution to the fighting on the ground, including the swift release of all hostages. The tragic developments we are witnessing clearly demonstrate that this protracted conflict cannot and will not be resolved by force alone. At the same time, I wish to reiterate my country's firm commitment to Israel's right to defend itself in full compliance with international law and international humanitarian law. Nevertheless, we cannot remain silent in the face of the dire reality on the ground. And we urge all sides, including the Israeli authorities, to take every measure possible to facilitate the unimpeded delivery of humanitarian assistance to the civilian population in Gaza. Mr. President, we indeed support many aspects of this resolution, particularly those explicitly aimed at addressing humanitarian needs in Gaza. Yet, the resolution regrettably goes well beyond its stated humanitarian objective by incorporating some highly politically charged and even one-sided assertions. First and foremost, while we acknowledge that for the first time this General Assembly resolution explicitly refers to Hamas, specifically in relation to the hostages currently held captive, We deeply regret that the text once again fails to unequivocally condemn Hamas' unspeakable atrocities of 7 October, carried out with the deliberate intent to murder innocent civilians, including women and children. Let us be absolutely clear. Hamas bears responsibility for countless atrocities, including perpetrating violence against Gaza's civilian population, cynically using civilians as human shields and diverting humanitarian aid for its own ends. Mr. President, the irrefutable truth remains that Hamas terrorists could immediately bring this brutal conflict to an end by laying down their arms and releasing all remaining hostages. Mr. President, in light of these considerations, we decided to abstain from voting on this resolution. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Zechia. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative from New Zealand.

Thank you, President. New Zealand supported this resolution after careful consideration. We did so because a ceasefire in Gaza is desperately needed. Hamas's actions on and since 7 October 2023 are completely unconscionable and must be condemned unequivocally. Hamas's continued refusal to release the hostages they are holding is immoral and a barrier to progress on the situation. New Zealand has rightly designated Hamas in its entirety as a terrorist entity. At the same time, the humanitarian situation in Gaza is intolerable and the world's patience has run out. As New Zealand has said consistently, this crisis must end. The excuses Israel has used for the ongoing suffering of innocent civilians are no longer credible. It is imperative that all parties comply with their obligations under international law. Israel is clearly required by international humanitarian law to provide for the basic needs of civilians in Gaza, and to facilitate unimpeded humanitarian access. The protection of civilians, humanitarian personnel, and medical workers is essential. Like many members of the international community, New Zealand has already taken a range of measures in respect of this conflict. This resolution does not impose any new obligations on New Zealand. We reiterate our call for the parties to urgently return to a ceasefire. New Zealand will continue to advocate for meaningful progress towards a two-state solution, which remains the only blueprint for peace we have. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of New Zealand. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative for Bulgaria.

Mr. President, Bulgaria supported the resolution on protection of civilians and upholding legal and humanitarian obligations, reflecting our deep concern with the ongoing violence in Gaza and the worsening humanitarian crisis on the ground. The suffering of civilians, especially children and vulnerable persons, is unacceptable and must end. We fully support the language in the resolution on the protection of the humanitarian workers and the UN personnel. Bulgaria strongly condemns the attacks on the humanitarian personnel and recalls that civilian protection is a core legal obligation, not an option. We therefore call for all parties to respect and strictly implement the international law, including international humanitarian law. Bulgaria reiterates its unconditional condemnation of the heinous October 7th terrorist attacks perpetrated by Hamas. There can be no justification for such brutality. We insist on the immediate, dignified, and unconditional release of all hostages held by Hamas and other terrorist groups. We therefore welcome the language in the resolution reaffirming the legal prohibition of hostage taking under international law and the obligation to release hostages. We regret, however, that the resolution fails to unequivocally condemn Hamas' brutal terrorist attack on 7 October, which the international community must denounce without any ambiguity. The international targeting of civilians, use of terror and hostage-taking are blatant violations of international law and the perpetrators must be held accountable. Bulgaria adds its voice to the call for upholding international law, recalls the need to fully implement the decisions and orders of the international courts, and will continue to oppose any attempts to politicization of the international judicial institutions. In closing, allow me to once again reaffirm Bulgaria's longstanding principled support for the two-state solution. The vision of Israel and Palestine coexisting side by side can only be achieved if Hamas is excluded from playing any role in the future of Gaza. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Bulgaria. I will now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Germany.

Thank you, Mr. President. Germany voted in favor of the resolution. We took this decision after careful considerations and numerous consultations, including at ministerial level with partners. Some, such as Italy, will also take the floor later for an explanation of vote. We once again unequivocally condemn the horrific attacks carried out by Hamas and other terrorist groups on October 7th, 2023. Horrific attacks against innocent civilians. These attacks are unjustifiable. We call on the General Assembly to do the same, and we would have preferred to see corresponding language in this resolution. Mr. President, Israel has every right to defend itself against attacks within the limits of international law. It is our firm conviction in order to improve the situation in Gaza, three things are urgently needed: an immediate return to a ceasefire, the immediate release of the hostages, and the unimpeded flow of humanitarian aid to Gaza. We are extremely worried about the fate of the hostages who continue to be held by Hamas and other terrorist groups in inhumane conditions. Hamas must release all hostages and Hamas must lay down its arms immediately and unconditionally. There can be no future for Gaza with Hamas, neither in government nor militarily, and Hamas must be held accountable for its crimes. The use of civilian infrastructure for military purposes and any misuse of humanitarian assistance is utterly unacceptable. But Hamas cannot be defeated by military means alone. What is needed above all is a long-term political plan for the future of Gaza after the war. We are convinced that the two-state solution is the only realistic path that can allow both Israelis and Palestinians to coexist in peace, sovereignty, security, and dignity, and it is also the only path towards lasting peace and stability in the region Germany fully supports the realization of the right of the Palestinian people to self-determination and their legitimate aspirations to establish their own state our approach is to help build the Palestine state every single day by developing and strengthening its foundation and future institutions through financial and technical cooperation at the same time, Mr. President Germany bears a special responsibility for Israel and for Israel's security. We firmly believe that the vision of an independent, democratic and viable Palestinian state can only be achieved through negotiations. Germany is working actively and constructively with the international community toward this goal. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Germany I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of China.

President, I thank you for holding today's emergency special session of the GA. China voted in favor of the draft resolution. It has already been 19 months since the outbreak of the conflict in Gaza. Over 55,000 people in Gaza have lost their lives. Over two million people are deeply trapped in an unprecedented humanitarian catastrophe. The conflict has become a stain on human civilization. Last week, the ten elected members of the Security Council put forth a draft resolution on humanitarian issues in Gaza, which enjoyed the support of 14 Council members, yet was once again vetoed by the US. China finds this deeply disappointing and regrettable. The draft resolution of the GA just adopted reflects the overwhelming call of the international community, sends a strong political message and embodies the solidarity and consensus among the overwhelming majority of Member States. We must not continue to allow innocent civilians to die. Israel continues to escalate its military offensive on Gaza and each day large numbers of innocent lives are lost. Whatever pretext will not make killing civilians noble or just. Cruel facts have already made clear that force will not bring peace and prolonging the war will only lead to more deaths and hatred. An immediate and permanent ceasefire is the right way to save lives and to get the hostages home. We urge Israel to immediately stop all its military operations in Gaza. The country with significant influence on the party concerned should adopt an impartial and responsible attitude and take effective and strong action. We must not continue to allow the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza to worsen The UN and other humanitarian agencies have sounded the alarm many times that large-scale famine is imminent in Gaza. In contrast, outside the borders of Gaza, massive amounts of food are piled in warehouses, yet it's impossible to deliver them to the starving civilians. Such forced deprivation of the right of the people to subsistence supplies is in violation of IHL, cruel and unacceptable. The UN has already pointed out that the mechanism for distributing humanitarian supplies promoted by the US and Israel goes against the principles of impartiality, independence, and neutrality. is inadequate for easing the humanitarian situation and will instead put civilians in greater danger. China firmly opposes the weaponization of humanitarian aid and urges Israel to fulfill its obligations as the occupying power by immediately lifting the blockade on Gaza, fully restoring access for humanitarian supplies, and supporting the UN and other humanitarian agencies in carrying out their work. We must not continue to allow the foundation of multilateralism to be eroded. Since the outbreak of the conflict, the GA and the Security Council have adopted multiple resolutions requesting a ceasefire, and the ICJ has issued multiple orders on provisional measures, yet none of them has been effectively implemented. Full implementation of Security Council resolutions is an obligation on all member states under the UN Charter. Abiding by international law and IHL is a responsibility incumbent on all countries. The international community should take necessary actions to stop all violations of law and ensure accountability so as to jointly uphold multilateralism and the authority of international law. President, implementing the two-state solution is the only viable way out for the Palestinian question. Next week, we'll witness the high-level conference for the implementation of the two-state solution. We expect the conference to adopt practical and effective outcomes and to inject fresh momentum into the prospects of realizing the two-state solution. China will join efforts with the international community to continue to work for a ceasefire in Gaza, ease the humanitarian catastrophe, and ultimately achieve the comprehensive, just, and lasting settlement of the Palestinian question. I thank you, President.
I thank the distinguished representative of China. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Australia.

Thank you, President.

Australia voted in favour of this resolution because we want to see an immediate return to a ceasefire in Gaza, the unconditional and immediate release of hostages, adherence to international humanitarian law by all parties

and rapid, sustained and unimpeded humanitarian access.

While we do not agree with

everything in this resolution, our vote today reflects our commitment to working with the international community to end this conflict.

Australia remains unequivocal in our condemnation of Hamas and its abhorrent attacks on 7 October 2023 and all ongoing acts of terror.

Terrorist group Hamas must release all hostages immediately, unconditionally and with dignity.

And we demand the hostages are given humane treatment, including freedom from any form of torture or abuse and

access to health care.

Australia is disappointed that today's resolution failed to condemn Hamas. There can be no role for Hamas in the future governance of Gaza. President, civilians are being killed by the thousand. Children are starving. We need to come together to ensure that we support a two-state solution, which remains the only pathway to enduring peace and security for Israeli and Palestinian

people.

Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Australia. I give the floor to the distinguished representative of Sierra Leone.

Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President, Sierra Leone voted in favor of the resolution. In doing so, we join the overwhelming majority in this Assembly in expressing deep alarm at the continuing and worsening humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza. Over two million civilians have endured weeks of siege, bombardment, and blockade, with grave and devastating consequences. The territory now confronts the prospect of famine, after more than 11 weeks of total siege and severe restrictions on the flow of food, water, fuel, and medical supplies. Humanitarian reports indicate that Israeli security forces, strikes, and ground operations have killed tens of thousands of Palestinians, overwhelmingly civilians, including women and children. Under international law, No circumstance permits the deliberate starvation or collective punishment of a civilian population. The Fourth Geneva Convention and the established norms of customary international law strictly prohibit the use of starvation as a method of warfare. The systemic deprivation of basic life-saving resources is unequivocally unlawful. In this context, So, I only recall the binding provisional measures issued by the International Court of Justice in the case of South Africa versus Israel. The court ordered Israel to allow the unimpeded provision of urgent humanitarian assistance and to refrain from any action, I quote, calculated to bring about the Palestinian group's physical destruction in whole or in part, end of quote. Under the 1948 Genocide Convention, All states are obliged not only to refrain from acts of genocide, but to prevent and punish such crime. The State of Israel is legally bound to comply with these measures. Any denial of life-saving aid or attacks on civilians constitute a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions and may amount to a war crime. Mr. President, in the Security Council, Sierra Leone has consistently underscored the gravity of this crisis. At our most recent briefing on the situation in the Middle East, we reflected on our national experience, and we affirm our deep understanding of the consequences of delayed or insufficient international action. We recall with solemn clarity the collective failure to prevent the atrocities committed in Rwanda and Srebrenica. now formally recognized as genocide by competent international courts. These painful precedents underscore the cost of inaction. The ICJ's rulings reaffirm the binding legal and moral obligation of all states to act decisively to prevent genocide. The duty to prevent genocide is not discretionary. It is a preemptive norm of international law, use cogent binding upon all states. This duty requires not only abstention from such crimes, but the taking of timely, active, and effective measures to avert them. Today, we face a moment of equal grave consequence. We are alarmed by credible and persistent reports of indiscriminate bombardment, the destruction of essential civilian infrastructure, the obstruction of humanitarian access, and inflammatory rhetoric. Together, these acts and omissions may contribute to creating conditions of life intended to bring about the destruction of a group in whole or in part, conduct expressly prohibited by the Genocide Convention. Mr. President, when CENL joined our elected council members in co-pending a draft resolution focused on addressing Gaza's worsening humanitarian crisis, We did so in full alignment with the ICJ's determination that Gaza's population must not be deprived of humanitarian assistance. Regrettably, despite its purely humanitarian focus, the draft resolution, aptly described by the E10 coordinator as the bare minimum, was vetoed by one permanent member, even as all 14 others voted in favor. Surely, silence or inaction in the face of mass atrocities must never be normalized. When the Security Council is paralyzed by the use of the veto, it falls to this General Assembly to act, and has rightly done so today. Sierra Leone fully supports the resolution's call for the protection of civilians and the unimpeded provision of humanitarian assistance. We also express grave concern at the recent interdiction of the United Kingdom-flagged humanitarian vessel Madeline by Israeli naval forces, reportedly in international waters. The ship carrying aid and civilian volunteers, as reported, was seized hundreds of kilometers from Gaza. Such actions violate the law of the sea and customary international law, which grant flag states exclusive jurisdiction on the high seas. Even where blockades are recognized under international law, they must not be used to starve civilian populations or obstruct humanitarian relief. Mr. President, accountability is essential. The deliberate use of starvation, attacks on medical personnel or UN workers, and the destruction of civilian infrastructures are not only violations of Geneva Conventions, but they also impose conditions of life calculated to bring about destruction, prohibited under international law. This assembly must therefore invoke all lawful means, all lawful measures to uphold accountability and show respect for international law. Let us be clear. The rules which we invoke are acceptable as the rules developed and codified by the international community to promote peace and security, cooperation for development, and the protection of human dignity. Sadly, we do not invoke the rules today with expectation of compliance. The experience of our tenure on the Security Council makes clear that compliance is unlikely in the absence of credible pressure from those with the means and leverage to ensure it. We therefore view with grave concern the growing practice of dismissing legal obligations as optional, of subordinating humanitarian imperatives for short-term political objectives, and of undermining the very institutions and instruments designed to uphold peace. Mr. President, throughout, Sierra Leone has reaffirmed the centrality of a political solution We reiterate our steadfast support for a genuine two-state solution, the only just and sustainable outcome. Ending the occupation and blockade and implementing a just peace in accordance with international law and UN resolution is essential. The state of Israel and the Palestinian state must live side by side in security and dignity. This is the only path to lasting peace in the Middle East. In closing, Tehran calls on all UN member states and parties to the conflict to honor their international obligations. We urge the state of Israel to comply fully with the ICJ's provisional measures, the Geneva Conventions and the Genocide Convention, including by allowing full aid and the protection of civilians. We demand that Hamas and all armed groups to refrain from targeting civilians or using human shield or using them as human shields and to release the hostages. This Assembly must send a clear message that the protection of civilians and adherence to international law are paramount. The Assembly has done so by adopting the resolution. I thank you, Mr. President.
I thank the distinguished representative of Sierra Leone. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of the Kingdom of the Netherlands.

Mr President, I thank you for convening today's ESS and I have the honour to deliver this explanation of vote on behalf of the Kingdom of the Netherlands. The Kingdom of the Netherlands voted in favour of the resolution. Our position is clear. The current cycle of violence is not the way forward, for the sake of the hostages, the Palestinians and for Israel. We therefore regret the veto cast in the Security Council. Mr. President, we condemn the humanitarian blockade of Gaza, which is contrary to international humanitarian law, and we call on Israel to immediately resume rapid, safe, and unhindered access to Gaza for humanitarian aid and basic services, including electricity. Humanitarian aid should never be militarized or used as political leverage and should be compatible with the humanitarian principles of neutrality, impartiality and independence. We underline the critical importance of full, safe access for professional mandated humanitarian organizations, including the United Nations, the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement and their partners, to reach all people in need across Gaza. We urgently recall Resolution 2417, adopted with landmark expression of unity. This resolution strongly condemns the use of starvation of civilians as a method of warfare, which is prohibited by international humanitarian law, and that it may constitute a war crime. This current resolution can be an important step towards a necessary permanent ceasefire. We urge all parties to commit to the continuation of the negotiations so that all hostages can be released immediately and unconditionally and humanitarian aid can be delivered to those in need. Only then can a lasting solution that has the support of both parties and for which the two state solution remains the basis be achieved. An independent, viable Palestinian state existing alongside a secure Israel is the only way this conflict can be resolved. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of the Kingdom of the Netherlands. I give the floor to the distinguished representative of Italy.

Thank you, Mr President, Excellencies, distinguished colleagues. Italy voted in favour of the resolution before the General Assembly today on the humanitarian situation in Gaza. We took this decision after careful consideration and consultation at ministerial level, including with some who already took the floor, such as Germany. It has been 20 months since the heinous attacks by Hamas against innocent civilians in Israel. Hamas is responsible for what is currently happening in Gaza. The strip is now only rubble, desolation, and despair. Hostages are still being held by Hamas and other terrorist groups while their families are wasting away, losing hope by the day to hug them again. Hamas does not care for the welfare of the people of Gaza. For years, it has abused the rights of the citizens of Gaza persecuted opponents and used their resources not to improve their lives but to prepare to unleash this tragedy on them. In the current crisis, Hamas is turning its people mercilessly into human shields and starving them. Let there be no mistakes about it. In this situation, the only solution to exit this deadlock is a diplomatic one. The only way to release the hostages passes through diplomacy. Here too, Hamas seeks to preserve its own rule, not to improve on the predicament of the people of Gaza. We recognize the inherent right of Israel to self-defense, and we strongly reiterate the imperative to take all the hostages back home. Such objectives could, however, be realistically achieved only with an immediate ceasefire that would also alleviate the immense suffering of the Gazan civilians. It is essential that the territories of the Strip are made accessible to the action of international organizations, making it possible to resume full and unimpeded humanitarian assistance to the people of Gaza based on the respect of the rules of international humanitarian law. With today's resolution, the international community addresses those points, focusing on the indispensable humanitarian efforts to end the civilian misery, release the hostages and prevent further loss of life in Gaza. Of course, no resolution is perfect. We would have preferred to see in the text a clear condemnation of Hamas for all the above mentioned reasons, or a paragraph spelling that hostage taking and the use of civilians as human shields are unequivocally against international humanitarian law. Notwithstanding those lacunae, we decided nonetheless to vote yes because of the overarching objective to get an immediate ceasefire sparing innocent civilians, innocent women and children's lives, and making sure that humanitarian assistance is supplied immediately at scale and safely. Attaining this objective should also involve finding a solution to the Palestinian question. Italy firmly believes in a two state solution whereby two states, Israel and Palestine, live in peace, dignity and security within internationally recognised borders and two people, Israelis and Palestinians, have an equal right to exist and thrive. Italy will continue to work relentlessly towards this objective, also by co-chairing with Indonesia the working group on security for Israelis and Palestinians in the framework of the conference on the two-state solution from June 17 to June 20. Thank you, Mr. President.
I thank the distinguished representative of Italy Now I give the floor to the distinguished representative of Thailand.

Mr. President, Thailand voted in favor of this resolution because of our firm conviction that to address the urgent humanitarian crisis in Gaza is not only a moral imperative, but also a fundamental responsibility of the international community. Thailand remains deeply concerned about the dire humanitarian situation in Gaza and echoes the urgent appeal for the immediate safe and unhindered delivery of humanitarian assistance to all civilians in need. The UN personnel and humanitarian aid workers must be protected by all parties. The role of the UNRWA is critical to providing essential services and much needed assistance, as well as to protect the rights and dignity of the Palestine people. We call upon the international community to render support for its vital work. As we strengthen our collective humanitarian efforts, Thailand reiterates the urgent need for the international community to adopt a constructive approach towards achieving a lasting and sustainable peace in the region. Thailand urges all parties involved in the conflict to engage in diplomatic efforts to secure an immediate and durable ceasefire. the unconditional release of all remaining hostages, and the resumption of meaningful dialogue. We support the continued efforts of all parties concerned towards achieving a peaceful solution to the conflict with the realization of the two-state solution by which the states of Israel and Palestine live side by side in peace and security in accordance with international law and the relevant United Nations resolutions. Lasting peace and stability in the Middle East must be supported by the creation of sustainable livelihoods and the promotion of the well-being of the Palestinian people. Thailand welcomes ongoing efforts toward the recovery and reconstruction of Gaza. We take this opportunity to reaffirm our determination to take part in this reconstruction and long-term development endeavors. which are crucial for ensuring a viable and prosperous future of the State of Palestine. In conclusion, Thailand once again reiterates its unwavering commitment to humanitarian efforts, as reflected in our vote today. We hope that this resolution will pave the way for an enduring peace and the end of the suffering of all peoples in the region. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Thailand I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Cyprus.

As a matter of principle, Cyprus reaffirms its commitment to the full protection of all civilians. Moreover, Cyprus supports that all parties to armed conflicts must comply with their obligations under international law, including the UN Charter, international humanitarian law, and international human rights law. This is why we voted in favor of the resolution. Notwithstanding this, we wish to make the following points. Cyprus unequivocally condemns the heinous terrorist attacks by Hamas on October 7th. And in this regard, we acknowledge the legitimate security concerns of Israel and its right to self-defense in line with international law. We also join the calls for the resumption of negotiations for a lasting and permanent ceasefire, which will entail the release of all hostages. All restrictions must be lifted to enable the immediate reestablishment of safe, sustained, and unimpeded flow of humanitarian assistance at scale for the civilians in Gaza. Mr. President, ultimately, the only sustainable way forward that meets the security concerns and needs of the legitimate stakeholders is reviving the Middle East peace process on the basis of a two-state solution in line with the UN resolutions. We will continue actively supporting this aim of achieving enduring conditions of peace and dignity, equally for Israelis and Palestinians alike, as well as for fostering long-term stability in the Middle East as a whole. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Cyprus. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of the Marshall Islands.

President, I wish to provide a short statement and explanation of our vote on resolution L34. This resolution is now inadequate and this continued undertaking now dysfunctional, where we vote on nearly the same words in repetition. Many in our remote Pacific Islands care deeply about what's happening and taking place in Gaza and Israel. Stories handed down by generations before us about World War II, the death, devastation, sufferings, and hunger visited upon our people and islands are part of our history. So while we may be a small speck of islands on the other side of the world and far from what's happening in Gaza and Israel, having experienced war, we know and we do care deeply about the humanitarian sufferings and the security issues raised in this resolution. Resolution 34 addresses the current humanitarian crisis in the occupied Palestine and in particular Gaza. It calls for the ceasefire to resume and for accountability regarding violations of international law for all parties, including international humanitarian law with regards to the denial of access to humanitarian aid and the use of starvation as a method of warfare. Last year, the UN Security Council passed a resolution nearly identical to this one before the General Assembly today. This resolution today, just like the UN Security Council resolution, reflects a humanitarian and legal consensus. Consensus, and today we remain without a clear endpoint to a ceaseless civilian tragedy in Gaza, and the need persists to fully resolve kidnap hostages and their remains. This resolution clearly states the due obligation under international law to deliver humanitarian aid unrestricted and without prescribing the distribution channel. That such a fundamental need for humanitarian survival becomes a patrol mask killing as of grave concern. Yet also of concern is any potential for Hamas to take part in aid diversion. Months become years of a human rights crisis and violations remain without international accountability and the same objective and factual evidence demanded elsewhere. Neither does the resolution bring itself to adequately reference the violent actions of Hamas on 7 October 2023, an entity which a majority of this body wants to find as a militant and terrorist organization. The complexity of Gaza as both a security issue and as a humanitarian crisis has to be more clearly addressed. We too join the chorus in emphasizing a two-state solution, as does the resolution. But we aren't going to return to the 2000 Camp David summit, nor return to the ceasefire as called for in this resolution, without a significant step change in political will and perspective by all key and necessary actors. Simply put, as a General Assembly, we may not be able to easily wish or vote our way to a ceasefire. The Marshall Islands support any and all effective efforts to address recovery and reconstruction and urges continued dialogue towards the final and joint products as well as how to jointly implement such approaches. And this crisis deserves leadership and pragmatic results before it continues to worsen and dissent. The dramatic scale of suffering deserves a more effective response than institutional volley between the General Assembly and the Security Council. Mr. President, for the foregoing reasons, we voted abstain on resolution 34. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of the Marshall Islands. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Ghana.

Mr. President, once again, the dire circumstances in the occupied Palestinian territory, especially the Gaza Strip, have imposed upon this Assembly the responsibility to resume the 10th Emergency Special Session of the General Assembly and the solemn duty to act, and act we have. Since the horrendous attacks by the Hamas militants against southern Israel on 7 October 2023, The world has witnessed with the greatest of concern the brutal, disproportionate, and inhumane response that has been rolled out against the entirety of the Palestinian population in Gaza. Indeed, Ghana condemned Hamas for the brutal killing of the 1,200 innocent Israeli citizens and continues to do so for its holding hostage many innocent lives. However, the response to the continued military hostilities against the people of Gaza and the blockage of humanitarian aid to almost two million people with grave consequences for their survival as a people can only be a resounding no more. Mr. President, for my delegation, the outcome of the vote this afternoon is a reflection that no matter how grim circumstances may appear to be, the world is always full of people ready to stand with what is right and to make their voices count. While Ghana takes careful note of the legitimate concerns of the State of Israel, the overriding interest of our common humanity and the necessity to restrain all actions within the limits of international law and the Charter of the United Nations compelled us to affirm strongly our unambiguous support for the resolution. We hold that this Assembly's decision today is a clear signal to Hamas that the international community does not tolerate its intransigent acts that run counter to the interests of the Palestinian people in Gaza. It must immediately and unconditionally release all hostages and take seriously all ongoing mediation efforts to activate the different phases of the broken ceasefire agreement that is now required more than ever. The future of the Palestinian people is at stake, and many of us here recognize it. But so also is the future of Israel and its people. Ghana therefore calls for both parties to seize the window of opportunity for peace that has narrowly been opened and to make determined efforts towards the immediate cessation of the conflict, the release of all hostages, the opening of access for humanitarian assistance, and the preservation of important pillars of promise that can restore a political horizon for a future dialogue, rebuilding and the creation of the foundations that would enable the evolution of a peace-loving Palestinian state to exist side by side with the state of Israel. Thus far, war, death and destruction have prevailed. But now, with the adoption of the resolution this afternoon, we must give peace its chance. I thank you very much.

I thank the distinguished representative of Ghana. We have heard the last speaker in explanation of vote for this meeting. We shall hear the remaining speakers at a later date to be announced. The meeting is adjourned.
